guard: the synthetic status-walk child installs its signal handlers before the parent sends SIGUSR1 or SIGUSR2
why: Manager.startAgent can expose a PID before the node child has registered its SIGUSR handlers.
Sending SIGUSR2 in that window takes the default terminate action; the next signal used to throw
ESRCH and abort the entire suite. A child-written marker is the actual readiness event, and every
signal send is a named cell so an unexpected death remains legible. #798: the quiet seat's
ensure-gone cleanup signals a pid found in a listing, so it must tolerate an already-exited child.
